Who is credited with discovering Indium?
Indium: Ferdinand Reich. Indium is a chemical element; its symbol is In and its atomic number is 49.
Who is credited with discovering Californium?
Californium: Stanley Gerald Thompson. Californium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Cf and atomic number 98.
Who is credited with discovering Fluorine?
Fluorine: Henri Moissan. Fluorine is a chemical element; it has symbol F and atomic number 9.
This is the most common genetic cause of dwarfism, typically producing short arms and legs with a normal-length torso and an enlarged head with a prominent forehead — what condition is it?
Achondroplasia is a genetic disorder whose primary feature is dwarfism.
Often caused by misaligned or unevenly focused eyes in early childhood, this is the most common cause of single-eye vision loss in kids and young adults, nicknamed 'lazy eye' — what condition is it?
Amblyopia is a disorder of sight in which the brain fails to fully process input from one eye and over time favors the other eye.
A physician who called medicine his lawful wife and literature his mistress, this Russian writer produced four stage classics and ranks among modernism's founders — who is he?
Anton Chekhov was Russian dramatist and author (1860–1904).
Which genus of early hominins, which lived in Africa during the Pliocene and Early Pleistocene, gave rise to the genera Homo, Paranthropus, and Kenyanthropus?
Australopithecus (-loh-; or, os-, from Latin australis southern 'grc' and (pthkos) ape) is a genus of early hominins that existed in Africa during the Pliocene and Early Pleistocene.
This red-orange compound, formed from the breakdown of heme, is further processed into pigments that give feces their brown color and urine its straw-yellow hue. What is it?
Bilirubin (BR) (adopted from German, originally bili, for bile, plus ruber, Latin for red) is a red-orange compound that occurs as the reduction product of biliverdin, a breakdown product of heme.

Named for its bread-like texture and potato-like flavor when cooked, this tropical tree fruit spread through Oceania via ancient seafaring migrations before European navigators brought Polynesian varieties to the Caribbean — which fruit?
Breadfruit (Artocarpus altilis) is a species of flowering tree in the mulberry and jackfruit family (Moraceae).
Discovered in 1940, this non-intoxicating compound extracted from cannabis is used medically as an anticonvulsant for two rare, severe forms of childhood epilepsy — what is it?
Cannabidiol (CBD) is a phytocannabinoid, one of 113 identified cannabinoids in Cannabis, along with tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), and accounts for up to 40% of the plant's extract.

The scientific study of matter's properties and behavior, this physical science occupies an intermediate position between physics and biology, sometimes called the central science. What is this field of study?
Chemistry is the scientific study of the properties and behavior of matter. Chemistry also addresses the nature of chemical bonds in chemical compounds.
Domed-backed little beetles that mostly hunt aphids, they wear aposematic spots to warn off predators and are named for 'lady' Mary — what's the scientific family?
Coccinellidae is a widespread family of small beetles.

Though Colin Maclaurin published special cases two years earlier, this determinant-based method for solving linear systems bears the name of the mathematician who generalized it in 1750 — what's it known as?
Cramer's rule is an explicit formula for the solution of a system of linear equations with as many equations as unknowns, valid whenever the system has a unique solution.

Distinguished from their one-leaved cousins by a pair of embryonic seed leaves, this classic angiosperm classification was shown by molecular science not to form a single evolutionary lineage — which plant group?
Dicotyledon (or, more rarely, dicotyls), are one of the two groups into which all the flowering plants (angiosperms) were formerly divided.
Born in North Carolina in 1983, this former NSA contractor leaked classified files exposing global surveillance programs after working for the CIA, Dell, and a defense contractor — name him?

Edward Snowden (born June 21, 1983) is a former United States National Security Agency (NSA) intelligence contractor who leaked classified documents revealing the existence of global surveillance programs.
Also called grain alcohol, this volatile compound with the formula C2H5OH is the active ingredient in every alcoholic beverage — what is it?
Ethanol (also called ethyl alcohol, grain alcohol, drinking alcohol, or simply alcohol) is an organic compound with the chemical formula CH3CH2OH.
This everyday bodily process — expelling gas from the intestines through the anus — has its own dedicated field of scientific study named after it: what's the term for the process itself?
Flatulence is the expulsion of gas from the intestines via the anus, commonly referred to as farting.
Ordained a priest in 1923, this Belgian physicist connected an expanding universe to Einstein's field equations and floated an early Big Bang hypothesis — who was he?
Georges Lemaître (lə-MET-rə; 17 July 1894 - 20 June 1966) was a Belgian Catholic priest, theoretical physicist, and mathematician who made major contributions to cosmology and astrophysics.
Born Herman Webster Mudgett, this con artist and killer worked his crimes around the 1893 World's Columbian Exposition, earning the nickname "the Beast of Chicago" — who was he?
H. H. Holmes (May 16, 1861 - May 7, 1896), better known as Dr.

Often called the "father of the Indian nuclear programme," this theoretical physicist founded the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research and the research centre later renamed in his honour. Who was he?
Homi J. Bhabha (30 October 1909 - 24 January 1966) was an Indian nuclear theoretical physicist who is widely credited as the "father of the Indian nuclear programme".

Dubbed the 'saviour of mothers,' this 19th-century Hungarian doctor demonstrated that a simple hygiene practice could drastically cut deaths from childbed fever, decades before germ theory was widely accepted — who is he?

Ignaz Semmelweis (1 July 1818 - 13 August 1865) was a Hungarian medical doctor and scientist of German descent who was an early pioneer of antiseptic procedures and was described as the "saviour of mothers".
Most of the flowers used by the global perfume industry for this fragrant genus of shrubs and vines are grown in a single Egyptian village. What plant is it?
Jasmine (botanical name: Jasminum) is a genus of shrubs and vines in the olive family of Oleaceae.
Diagnosed via corneal topography and linked to frequent eye rubbing and allergies, this progressive disorder causes the cornea to bulge into a cone shape — which eye condition?
Keratoconus is an eye disorder in which the cornea, the transparent front part of the eye, gradually thins and bulges outward into a cone shape.
Caused by Mycobacterium bacteria, this ancient nerve-damaging disease can dull a person's sense of pain so badly that unnoticed wounds cost them their fingers and toes — what is it?
Leprosy (HD), is a long-term infection by the bacterium Mycobacterium leprae or Mycobacterium lepromatosis.
Born in Vienna into one of Europe's richest families, this philosopher studied under Bertrand Russell at Cambridge and transformed 20th-century philosophy of language and logic — who is he?

Ludwig Wittgenstein ((h)tyne; Austrian; 26 April 1889 - 29 April 1951) was an Austro-British philosopher who worked in logic, philosophy of mathematics, philosophy of mind, and philosophy of language.

In 1835 she and Caroline Herschel became the first female Honorary Members of the Royal Astronomical Society, and decades later this Scottish polymath's name topped John Stuart Mill's women's-suffrage petition. Who is she?
Mary Somerville (ne Fairfax, formerly Greig; 1780-1872) was a Scottish scientist, writer, and polymath.
Entering Soviet service in 1983 alongside the larger Su-27, this 'Fulcrum' air-superiority fighter was later adapted into a multirole jet — which aircraft is it?
Mikoyan MiG-29 (NATO reporting name: Fulcrum) is a twin-engine fighter aircraft designed in the Soviet Union.
When the radial fibres of the iris over-dilate the pupil beyond its normal light response, what do doctors call this condition?
Mydriasis is the dilation of the pupil, usually having a non-physiological cause, or sometimes a physiological pupillary response.
Nicknamed the 'winter vomiting disease' and the most common cause of gastroenteritis, this fecal–orally spread bug usually strikes about 24 hours after exposure. What is it?
Norovirus is the most common cause of gastroenteritis. Norovirus, also known as Norwalk virus, is the most common cause of gastroenteritis.
Making up most of Earth's crust, this class of chemical compounds pairs oxygen with at least one other element — even the thin protective skin on aluminum foil counts as one — what's the class?
Oxide is a chemical compound containing at least one oxygen atom and one other element in its chemical formula.
Named from Greek words for 'odd' and 'toe,' this mammalian order groups horses, rhinoceroses, and tapirs together based on their toe count. Which order?
Perissodactyla (from Ancient Greek, perisss 'odd' and, dktylos 'finger, toe'), or odd-toed ungulates, is an order of ungulates.

This common skin condition begins with a single scaly 'herald patch,' followed weeks later by an eruption of smaller pinkish spots, and typically clears on its own within three months. What is it called?
Pityriasis rosea is a type of skin rash.
Roaming the interior of western and central North America, this even-toed mammal survived the Pleistocene extinction of its close relatives and evolved to resemble an antelope — which creature is it?
Pronghorn (Antilocapra americana) is a species of artiodactyl (even-toed, hoofed) mammal indigenous to interior western and central North America.

Distinguished from their smaller rodent cousins mainly by size, these long-tailed rodents span dozens of genera worldwide, with Rattus being the most familiar — of the 56 known species, what are they collectively called?
Rat are various medium-sized, long-tailed rodents.

Originally bred in Germany to herd livestock and pull carts of butchered meat to market until railways took over in the mid-1800s, this medium-to-large mastiff-type dog now also works as a guard and police dog - name the breed?
Rottweiler (UK also) is a breed of domestic mastiff type dog, regarded as medium-to-large or large.
Made by Novo Nordisk and taken by injection or pill, this peptide medicine doubles as a diabetes treatment and a weight-management drug — what is it?
Semaglutide is an anti-diabetic medication used for the treatment of type 2 diabetes, and an anti-obesity medication used for weight management.

With the formula NaNO3 and historically mined in massive deposits in Chile, this white, deliquescent salt is a key industrial source used to make fertilizers, pyrotechnics, and explosives — which compound?
Sodium nitrate is the chemical compound with the formula NaNO3. The mineral form is also known as nitratine, nitratite or soda niter.

Tracing its lineage back to ancestral fish from the Early Jurassic period roughly 174 to 201 million years ago, this family of 27 fish species is one of only two living branches of an ancient order that also includes the paddlefish — name this fish family?
Sturgeon are the 27 species of fish belonging to the family Acipenseridae.

Named for the order of fish that includes pufferfish, this potent neurotoxin also turns up in blue-ringed octopuses and rough-skinned newts, and is actually produced by symbiotic bacteria rather than the animals themselves — what's the toxin?

Tetrodotoxin (TTX) is a potent neurotoxin. Its name derives from Tetraodontiformes, an order that includes pufferfish, porcupinefish, ocean sunfish, and triggerfish; several of these species carry the toxin.
Not a single branch of the family of life but a strategy evolved over and over — a tall trunk and branches reaching for sunlight — describes which kind of perennial plant?
Tree is a perennial plant with an elongated stem, or trunk, usually supporting branches and leaves.

This flowering plant genus, the largest in its family with over 680 species, is found mostly across the temperate Northern Hemisphere but also as far-flung as Hawaii and the Andes. What is this plant commonly called?
Viola (plant) is a genus of flowering plants in the family Violaceae.
This mosquito-borne viral disease causes chills, nausea, and muscle pain, and in about 15% of cases progresses to liver damage that turns the skin a telltale color — what disease is it?
Yellow fever is a viral disease of typically short duration.
This class of bony fish accounts for nearly 99% of all living fish species, ranging in size from an 8-millimeter minnow to a giant sunfish weighing 2,700 kilograms — what is it?
Actinopterygii: Class of ray-finned bony fishes.
Its very name comes from the Arabic for 'the kohl,' and chemically it's any compound carrying a hydroxyl group on a saturated carbon — a family that ranges from methanol to cholesterol. What is it?
Alcohol (chemistry): Organic compound with at least one hydroxyl (–OH) group.
Formed when hydrogen atoms in ammonia are swapped out for carbon-based groups, which class of nitrogen-containing organic compounds includes aniline as its simplest aromatic member?
Amine: Chemical compounds and groups containing nitrogen with a lone pair (:N)
Awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2008 for his AIDS-relief work on PEPFAR, this immunologist directed the U.S. allergy and infectious-disease institute from 1984 to 2022. Who is he?
Known as common wormwood, this bitter herb native to North Africa and temperate Eurasia lends its name and flavor to a notorious green spirit — which plant?
Artemisia absinthium: Species of plant. It is grown as an ornamental plant and is used as an ingredient in the spirit absinthe and some other alcoholic beverages.
Blooming for weeks each spring and thriving in the shade under trees, these flowering shrubs belong to the genus Rhododendron — what are they called?
Azalea: Subgroup of rhododendron flowering shrubs.
A likely hybrid of lemon and a bitter citrus relative, this fragrant fruit flavors tea, snus, and perfume, though it can heighten skin's sensitivity to sunlight — which fruit?
Originally launched as the McDonnell Douglas MD-95, this narrow-body airliner seats up to 134 passengers with twin engines mounted at the tail — which jet?
Ranging from roughly seawater-strength up to a fully saturated 26%, which salty solution is used for pickling food, de-icing roads, and turns up as a wastewater byproduct of desalination?
Brine: Concentrated solution of salt in water.
Named to honor the Virgin Mary and her golden crown, this daisy-family flower is also known as the pot marigold — which plant?
Calendula officinalis: Species of flowering plant in the daisy family Asteraceae.
Known also as yoke elm, this species of hornbeam native to Western Asia and Europe grows only up to elevations of about 1,000 metres — which species?
Carpinus betulus: Species of tree. It requires a warm climate for good growth, and occurs only at elevations up to 1,000 metres (3,300 ft).
Often called 'the father of the computer,' this English polymath designed the difference engine and the analytical engine, borrowing a punch-card principle from the Jacquard loom — who is he?
Charles Babbage: English mathematician, philosopher, and engineer (1791–1871)
One of the original citrus fruits, this large fragrant relative of the lemon has a thick, coarse rind and is a genetic ancestor of most modern citrus hybrids — what is it?

This medium-sized bird of prey ranges across Europe into northwestern China, hunting rodents like voles from a perch, with northern populations migrating as far as South Africa for winter — what bird is this?
Common buzzard: Species of bird of prey. It is a member of the genus Buteo in the family Accipitridae.

This blood-feeding parasitic insect, scientifically Pthirus pubis, typically lives in coarse body hair and diverged from a gorilla-infecting relative about 3.3 million years ago — what is it commonly called?
Crab louse: Species of insect. The crab louse or pubic louse (Pthirus pubis) is an insect that is an obligate ectoparasite of humans, feeding exclusively on blood.
This Swedish tech entrepreneur founded and chairs a streaming giant, with a net worth estimated at $8.7 billion in December 2025 — who is he?
Named from the Latin word for 'finger' and best known through the common foxglove species, which plant genus produces tall spikes of tubular, often purple flowers?
Digitalis: Genus of flowering plants in the family Plantaginaceae.
Marked by itchy 1-2mm blisters on the palms and soles that clear in three to four weeks but often return, this form of dermatitis has no known cause — what is it?
Dyshidrosis: Inflammatory disease of the skin in humans.
The tallest and heaviest of all living penguins, this flightless Antarctic bird can top 45 kilograms and sports bright-yellow ear patches — which species is it?
Emperor penguin: Large flightless seabird endemic to Antarctica.
This Marine-turned-professor's 1981 memoir about fighting at Peleliu and Okinawa later inspired Ken Burns's The War and HBO's The Pacific, where he was played by Joseph Mazzello — who is he?
Made up mostly of undigested food broken down by gut bacteria, this bodily waste is expelled through the anus and can even be dried for fuel or used as fertilizer — what is it?
Feces: Solid or semisolid remains of undigested food.

First described by 19th-century French psychiatrists Charles Lasègue and Jules Falret, this rare condition — also called shared psychotic disorder — lets one person's delusion spread to another. What is it called?

Folie à deux: Shared psychosis, a psychotic disorder. The disorder, first conceptualized in 19th century French psychiatry by Charles Lasègue and Jules Falret, is also known as Lasègue–Falret syndrome.

Named after Scottish naturalist Alexander Garden and first proposed in 1753 by botanist Jane Colden, this fragrant flowering genus in the coffee family is native to Africa, Asia and Australia — which plant genus?
Gardenia: Genus of flowering plants in the coffee family Rubiaceae.
Nicknamed the blue dragon, this pelagic sea slug floats upside down using surface tension and a stomach gas bubble, and feeds on the Portuguese man o' war — what is it?

Nicknamed for its mole-like digging forelegs and dense fur, this insect widespread across Europe and introduced to the eastern United States is a textbook example of convergent evolution — which species?
Gryllotalpa gryllotalpa: Species of cricket-like animal.

Formally described only in 1983, this helical, flagella-driven bacterium burrows through the stomach's mucous lining and is the chief culprit behind gastric ulcers and some stomach cancers. What is it?
Nicknamed 'Hobbit,' this extinct species of small archaic humans stood about 1.1 meters tall and lived on the Indonesian island of Flores until roughly 50,000 years ago — which species?
Homo floresiensis: Extinct small human species found in Flores.

Typically begun with an induction of preliminary instructions, this state of focused attention and heightened suggestibility is debated as either an altered trance or a form of imaginative role-play — what is it?
Hypnosis: State of increased suggestibility. There are competing theories explaining hypnosis and related phenomena.

This neurological emergency is sudden bleeding directly into brain tissue or its fluid-filled cavities — not from a blocked vessel, but a burst one — causing anything from headache to sudden paralysis. What is it?
Intracerebral hemorrhage: Type of intracranial bleeding that occurs within the brain tissue itself.
Enlisting disguised as a man named 'Jean' on Bougainville's expedition, this expert botanist became the first woman to circumnavigate the globe — who is she?
Jeanne Baret: French explorer, naturalist, botanist (1740–1807)

This Indian aerospace engineer led the nation's space agency as chairman and served as secretary of the Department of Space, after directing both the Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre and the Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre — who is he?
Once a water retriever in Italy's Po Delta marshlands, this Italian dog breed later became prized for sniffing out truffles — which breed?
Lagotto Romagnolo: Italian breed of dog.
As a principal shareholder of L'Oréal, this French heiress was the richest woman in the world at the time of her death in 2017, worth $44.3 billion — who was she?
Liliane Bettencourt: French heiress, socialite and businesswoman (1922–2017)
Originating in 1993 and written in ANSI C, this lightweight scripting language was designed to be embedded inside other applications — which language?
Lua: Lightweight programming language. Lua is a lightweight, high-level, multi-paradigm programming language designed mainly for embedded use in applications.
Sharing joints only with the temporal bones, this is the skull's lone movable bone, hosting the lower teeth and shrinking in size since humans began farming around 10,000 BCE — what is it called?
Mandible: Lower jaw bone. The mandible hosts the lower teeth (their depth delineated by the alveolar process).

This elephant-sized extinct genus of South American ground sloths, whose type species weighed up to four tonnes, was first identified from a fossil found on an Argentine riverbank in 1787 — which genus?
Megatherium: Genus of extinct ground sloth. The first (holotype) specimen of Megatherium americanum was discovered in 1787 on the bank of the Luján River in what is now northern Argentina.
North of the Arctic Circle in summer, this phenomenon keeps the sky lit long after the clock strikes twelve — what is it called?
Midnight sun: Natural phenomenon when daylight lasts for a whole day.
Sold under the brand name Singulair, this asthma medication blocks leukotriene D4 in the lungs but received a UK black box warning in 2019 over neuropsychiatric side effects — what is it?
Montelukast: Medication used in asthma or COPD.
This genus of venomous elapid snakes across Africa and Asia is home to the 'true cobras' — after a 2009 taxonomic revision folded in two other genera, it now contains 38 species — which genus?
Naja: Genus of snakes. Until recently, the genus Naja had 20 to 22 species, but it has undergone several taxonomic revisions in recent years, so sources vary greatly.
Colourless and odourless, this element pairs with itself to form a diatomic gas that makes up about 78% of the air you're breathing — what is it?
Nitrogen: Chemical element with atomic number 7 (N)

The most widely cultivated species of its genus, this bulb vegetable counts garlic, leeks and chives among its close relatives, and the shallot was reclassified as merely a variety of it in 2011 — what is it?
Onion: Bulbous vegetable. The shallot is a botanical variety of the onion which was classified as a separate species until 2011.
Nicknamed the 'scaly anteater,' this nocturnal mammal is covered in keratin scales and slurps up ants and termites with a long tongue — which animal?
Pangolin: Mammals of the order Pholidota.
Native to Asia, Europe, and western North America, this flowering shrub's fragrant blooms last just 7 to 10 days each spring — which plant?
Peony: Genus of flowering plants in the family Paeoniaceae.

Also known as physiography, this branch of natural science studies the atmosphere, hydrosphere, biosphere, and geosphere — as opposed to the branch focused on the built human environment. Which field of study?
Physical geography: Study of processes and patterns in the natural environment.
This large, structurally diverse family of plant compounds includes flavonoids and tannic acid, some of which were historically used as dyes and for tanning garments — what are they called?
Known by folk names like 'bird cherry' and 'Mayday tree,' this flowering plant in the rose family is native to Europe and northern Asia — what species is it?
Prunus padus: Species of flowering plant in the rose family.
What term describes an atom, molecule, or ion with at least one unpaired valence electron, making it highly reactive and prone to processes like dimerization or polymerization?
Radical (chemistry): Atom, molecule, or ion that has an unpaired valence electron; typically highly reactive.
Named from Greek words for 'rose' and 'tree,' this flowering shrub genus is Nepal's national flower and includes azaleas as a subgenus — which plant?
Rhododendron: Genus of flowering plants. Azaleas make up two subgenera of Rhododendron.
First identified in November 2002 and traced through civets to horseshoe bats in Yunnan, this viral respiratory disease had an 11% fatality rate before its outbreak ended in 2003 — which disease?
After early family-friendly Christian games found little success, which developer switched to horror in 2014 and created a hit franchise of horror video games?
Scott Cawthon: American video game developer (born 1978)

Adapted from the Army's Black Hawk with folding rotor blades and a hinged tail to fit aboard ships, this twin-engine Navy helicopter handles everything from anti-submarine warfare to medical evacuation — which aircraft?
The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom
Sikorsky SH-60 Seahawk: Naval helicopter series of the H-60/S-70 family.
Native to the tropical Americas and a cousin of the cherimoya, which spiny fruit smells like pineapple and tastes like strawberries and apple with a sour citrus tang?
Soursop: Tropical fruit tree. Soursop (also called graviola, guyabano, and in Hispanic America guanábana) is the fruit of Annona muricata, a broadleaf, flowering, evergreen tree.
A member of the rose family, this bright red treat is botanically not a berry at all, and each of its 'seeds' on the outside is really a tiny fruit called an achene — what is it?
Strawberry: Edible fruit. The garden strawberry (or simply strawberry; Fragaria × ananassa) is a widely grown hybrid plant cultivated worldwide for its fruit.

This mammal family includes true digging specialists as well as aquatic desmans and the water-and-tunnel-adept star-nosed species, absent from Ireland but found from Eurasia to as far south as tropical Southeast Asian mountains — which family?
Talpidae: Family of small insectivorous mammals.
A cousin of caffeine found in trace amounts in tea, coffee, and chocolate, which methylxanthine drug is used to treat asthma and COPD by blocking adenosine receptors?
Theophylline: Drug used to treat respiratory diseases.
This central part of the body, from which the head, neck, limbs, and tail extend, is divided into chest, abdomen, and pelvic segments — which body part?

Torso: Central part of the living body. The tetrapod torso — including that of a human — can be divided into segments:

The chest or upper torso.

A reddish-purple natural dye secreted by sea snails in the Muricidae family, also called royal purple or imperial dye. The colored compound is 6,6'-dibromoindigo, extracted from snails like Bolinus brandaris. What is this ancient dye?
Tyrian purple: Natural dye extracted from Murex sea snails. The name Tyrian refers to the city of Tyre in ancient Phoenicia (modern-day Lebanon).

The northernmost marsupial on Earth, this cat-sized nocturnal opportunist is a familiar visitor to trash cans and compost piles across North America, and often ends up as roadkill due to its slow pace — what is it?
Virginia opossum: Species of North American marsupial.
Aboard Apollo 8, the first crewed mission to leave low Earth orbit, this astronaut snapped the iconic "Earthrise" photograph as the crew circled the Moon ten times — who took it?
William Anders: American astronaut and lunar explorer (1933–2024)
The symbol for seaborgium is Sg. Seaborgium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Sg and atomic number 106.
The symbol for lanthanum is La. Lanthanum is a chemical element; it has symbol La and atomic number 57.

Ganapath: It stars Tiger Shroff in a dual role alongside Kriti Sanon, Elli AvrRam and Rahman, while Amitabh Bachchan appears in a cameo appearance.

The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring

The Boy in the Striped Pyjamas (film)

Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom

Love Actually is a 2003 Christmas romantic comedy film written and directed by Richard Curtis.
